caption: [@es3n1n](https://twitter.com/es3n1n) and I developed rCTF v2, an open-source platform for hosting cybersecurity capture-the-flag competitions. It is, objectively, the best work I have ever done, and is state-of-the-art in its capabilities.

In collaboration with pixel artist [@uarfun](https://twitter.com/uarfun), I designed the MaltaCTF landing page. The artwork itself is split into foreground/background to create a parallax effect, and is available in three variations: day, evening, and night. The variant you see on first load is based on your system time.

PCB badges I designed for MaltaCTF. The shiny logo is exposed copper with an ENIG (electroless nickel immersion gold) finish. The namebox is left as smooth white soldermask for easy writing with a marker.

Inspired by Hiroshi Yoshida's [time-of-day prints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroshi_Yoshida#Artistic_style), I made a 24-hour pixel-art timelapse of [Fälensee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A4lensee), a lake in eastern Switzerland. The composition was built and rendered entirely in Godot.

A picture of my home office. To emphasize function, I use a [Skådis](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/skadis-pegboard-white-10321618/) pegboard to hang high-use items, and have desk-mounted my monitor for more real estate. To emphasize personality, I use corkboard to showcase memorabilia, and the color complements the rubberwood finish I chose for my sit-stand desk. My MFF PC case has bamboo slits on its front panel to also support the natural warm palette.

As part of OtterSec’s CTF sponsorship program, I worked with [@uarfun](https://twitter.com/uarfun) to design collectible player cards for the teams we support. Players received bespoke pixel art based on their avatars, then chose two special abilities and their social links, plus a card color matching their main CTF category.

The landing I built for V12, an autonomous hacker/security review engine developed by the founders of [Zellic](https://zellic.io). I placed heavy emphasis on showcasing product functionality and took great care in its microanimations.
Unfortunately, hanging up posters is hard, so we chained lanyards together against a mezzanine railing at our venue to hang up this print of the event artwork.

A construction sheet and digital render of the logo I created for V12. The logo itself is inspired by the chrome embleming you see on the tail of a car. The entire logo can be neatly constructed with one unit ($x = 12$, with $y = 4x$) and three angles ($96^\circ, 72^\circ, 36^\circ$).
I worked with OpenAI and Paradigm on "EVM​bench", their state-of-the-art smart contract benchmark.
The landing I built for OtterSec, a leading blockchain security auditing firm. The hero section uses a no-dependency, vanilla JS shader.
For SekaiCTF 2026 I developed rCTF-luna, a custom theme attempting to faithfully recreate the aesthetic of "Project Sekai: Colorful Stage!".

The landing I designed for Zellic's (sunset) validators program. The artwork itself is true 1-bit (2-color), but a dimming layer was placed on top to emphasize light within the composition. Yes, I know it looks exactly like [Return of the Obra Dinn](https://obradinn.com/); this was a happy coincidence!
The landing I built for Hacktron, an AI-native security platform for code reviews and penetration tests.
The shirt I designed for MaltaCTF, which was printed on 280gsm heavy cotton with an acid wash. The backside was inspired by Maltese Cross gold coins.
I created "astro-erudite," a highly opinionated, unstyled static blogging template out of frustration with existing templates and obsession with perfection.
A collection of various teasers and promotional graphics I've made for SekaiCTF's social presence.
I contributed to BountyBench (accepted NeurIPS 2025), a cybersecurity benchmark that evaluates AI agents’ offensive-defensive capabilities with bug bounties.
For SekaiCTF 2023, I replicated the gacha system from "Project Sekai: Colorful Stage!" using exclusively Unity.

Mockups of duplexed, luxury business cards I designed for OtterSec. The card is printed on a soft, matte paper with a silver foil logo. On the content side, an oversized emblem is blind-debossed into the stock, and its silhouette can be emphasized with lights and shadows. The contact details carry shallow debossing.
A ridiculously cute VTuber-style sticker I made for OtterSec. The text reads "かわうそ / セキュリティ" (otter security).
I made the logo and docs site for Anchor v2, the leading Rust-based development framework for building secure smart contracts.

Graphics and maps I made for "[A Retrospective on 14 Nights in Japan](/blog/japan-retrospective)". The maps represent transit routes and were hand-drawn over screenshots of [Catenary Maps](https://maps.catenarymaps.org).

An assortment of merchandise I've made. In clockwise order, we have:
(1) An "ACCC" parody tee (for more context, see ["Smart Eyes, Stupid Hands"](/blog/smart-eyes-stupid-hands/)).
(2) A "CTF Iceberg" tee I made for LakeCTF, containing many cultural references and inside jokes.
(3) An "Otter University" collegiate hoodie, a gift for the end of our summer internship program. It has a custom embroidered emblem/crest.
(4) A gag tee parodying Abbey Road for Breakpoint London 2026.
